Every section of the workshop has a notebook. One more sits past the end of the
day, as a take-home deep dive. They are **English-primary**, and every heading
carries a one-line Spanish summary — *cada encabezado lleva un resumen en
español.*

## How they are built

Every notebook has the same five parts, so you always know where you are:

1. **Header** — the section title, its objectives, and an *Open in Colab* badge.
2. **Setup** — installs and imports only what this section needs, and loads its
   own data. Each notebook is self-contained: no local files, and no dependency
   on any other notebook.
3. **Explanation and code**, alternating. They build up, rather than dropping a
   wall of code on you.
4. **Exercises** — `# TODO` stubs taken from the handbook, each followed by a
   folded solution cell. Open it after you have tried.
5. **Closing** — the Kahoot check for that section, and a link back here.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
The notebooks are committed with **no outputs and no execution counts**. Every
number you see is one you produced. The prose quotes the expected results, so
you can tell whether yours are right. If yours differ, that is worth
investigating rather than dismissing.
:::

## Running them somewhere other than Colab

The notebooks only need the scientific Python stack. Locally:

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}.git
cd {{< var repo.name >}}
uv run --with numpy,pandas,matplotlib,scikit-learn,scikit-image,scipy,jupyterlab,ipywidgets jupyter lab
```

`matplotlib` and `ipywidgets` are in that list because every notebook plots, and
all but 00 use sliders. Both ship with Colab, so a missing one only shows up
when you run locally.

`scikit-learn` and `scikit-image` ship the tumour data, the handwritten digits
and the photographs. So sections 01, 03, 04, 06 and 09 run with no network at
all. The other nine notebooks each fetch one file the first time they run: a CSV
from GitHub, the storm video clip from Wikimedia, or a voice recording for
notebook 11's take-home E.
